turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - alloy_pair_target_train.csv: 300 samples described by composition in wt% — C, Mn, Si, Cr, Ni, Mo, V, Nb, Co, Al, Ti, Cu
      (Fe is the balance: Fe = 100 − Σ of the others) — plus processing parameters
      (solutionizing_temp, aging_temp, aging_time, cooling_rate) and categorical
      settings heat_treatment (annealed | quenched | quench_temper | solution_aged)
      and route (cast | wrought | AM), with the measured 0.2 % proof yield strength in MPa (the `target` column).
  - alloy_pair_target_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE recipes whose yield strength was NOT measured, with the same columns plus `candidate_id` and no `target`.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have a yield strength CLOSEST to 1051 MPa — not the highest, the closest to that value — then select the 5 best candidates from the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904, c905".
turns.answer_text:
The requested target, **1051 MPa, is above the largest measured training value (908.54 MPa)**, so this selection necessarily involves extrapolation.

The training data favour **quench-and-temper processing**, particularly wrought recipes with moderate alloy additions. Relevant high-strength examples include the **863.93 MPa** wrought sample solutionized at about **1111°C**, aged at **550°C**, and cooled at **28.9**, and the **908.54 MPa** quench-tempered sample solutionized at **1149°C** with cooling rate **38.3**.

My **similarity-based ranking** prioritizes candidates combining those favourable processing conditions with compositions near the stronger training recipes:

| Rank | Candidate | Main supporting features |
|---:|---|---|
| 1 | **c060** | Wrought, quench-tempered; solutionizing 1149°C, aging 551°C, cooling rate 37.9; moderate alloy additions. |
| 2 | **c099** | Similar processing window and balanced composition; somewhat shorter aging time. |
| 3 | **c052** | Solutionizing 1138°C, aging 535°C, 35-hour aging, cooling rate 34.9. |
| 4 | **c082** | Closely aligned processing conditions, with aging at 526°C and cooling rate 39.0. |
| 5 | **c049** | Favourable composition and cooling rate, but higher aging temperature, 589°C, makes it a less direct match. |

These are provisional candidates for approaching **1051 MPa**, not validated predictions that they reach it. Without a fitted and validated extrapolative model, their exact strengths—and consequently their order by absolute distance from 1051 MPa—remain uncertain.

Final: c060, c099, c052, c082, c049
